Marissa —

Quick review notes after looking at Maple_Resale_Cert.pdf:

- The form looks well completed for the purchaser side.
- For CA (Board of Equalization rules), we need the purchaser’s resale certificate (which they’ve provided) and seller identification. Redwood should record the seller’s name on our internal copy; notarization is not required in most CA transactions unless the seller requests it.
- For MA, we typically require the certificate to reference the applicable statute and include an effective date range; their PDF includes the statute reference but is missing the explicit effective start date.

Actions:
1) Ask Maple to add a single line with the effective start date (MM/DD/YYYY) — easiest path.
2) Confirm the seller name/EIN on our intake form. I’ll provide the Redwood seller info below so you can pass it to Emily to include if their form allows additional fields.

Redwood seller details (use exactly as below):
- Seller: Redwood Inference, Inc.
- Seller address: 220 Townsend St, San Francisco, CA 94107
- Seller EIN: 45-6789123

If Maple can re-upload the updated PDF, we can validate and notify finance to apply the tax-exempt status retroactively. If they prefer DocuSign, that’s fine — the key is the effective start date for MA.

Happy to take final sign-off after you get the updated file. I can loop in Legal if they want a second glance, but I don’t think it’s necessary.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
